tickets.title: Focusing and leaving a coordinate field rounds away authored precision, and the nudge inherits it
tickets.summary: MAJOR from the wave-119 verifier — PRE-EXISTING, reported by the T-700 slice while working beside it, and confirmed to reproduce by code-path analysis at every layer. attributes.rs `number_field`: :506 builds the display string as `format!("{}", value.round())`; :535 `on:focus` seeds the draft from that ROUNDED string; :539 `on:blur` calls `commit()` UNCONDITIONALLY; :516-523 `commit` parses the draft and calls `on_commit(n)` with no changed-check. Downstream `editor_ops::attrs_update_position` (:1293-1321) has NO equality skip — it calls `core.update_slot_position(...)` and then `after_local_edit()`. So the write is real and it mints an undo step. REPRO: place an entity by map drag so x = 412.37, click into the X field, click away WITHOUT TYPING -> the document holds 412. Tabbing through the Transform tab degrades every coordinate to an integer, dirties the mission and mints unmeant undo steps. THIS IS SILENT CORRUPTION OF AUTHORED PRECISION TRIGGERED BY AN IDLE CLICK. T-700 WIDENS THE BLAST RADIUS rather than causing it: the new PageUp/PageDown nudge seeds from the same rounded string, so nudging 412.37 commits 413, not 413.37 — the nudge inherits the rounding through `seed()`. All cited lines are unchanged context in the T-700 diff, so this is genuinely pre-existing; T-700 correctly declined to fix it because doing so changes commit behaviour well beyond its ticket. FIX, one line plus a pin: skip `on_commit` when the parsed draft equals the last settled value. That kills the no-op write, the rounding overwrite AND the extra undo step after a nudge in one change. Consider separately whether the DISPLAY should round at all, or should show the real value and only round for presentation — a field that displays a lie and then commits the lie is the deeper defect. Diagnosis: editor_verify/wave119.md MAJOR-2.
tickets.notes: filed by wave-119 adversarial verifier (editor factory)

tickets.title: Wave-119 residue: four census guards weaker than they read, and one mislabelled hit row
tickets.summary: Four NITs from the wave-119 verifier, grouped because each is a few lines and three are the same class — a guard that reads stronger than it asserts. Every underlying behaviour was independently verified correct; these are gaps in the guarantees. (1) eden_help.rs:953-961: `every_shared_channel_claimant_reads_live_state` is a per-listener SUBSTRING check, so an unrelated `get_untracked()` anywhere in the closure satisfies it. All ten current claimants genuinely gate their Escape path (the verifier read each), so this is latent — but the exemption it guards is the one that keeps a nine-claimant Escape channel legal, which is the last place a weak guard should sit. (2) eden_help.rs:1084-1094: `there_is_exactly_one_extractor` scans only the six declared surface files plus eden_help, so a fifth copy elsewhere in the crate would pass. A repo-wide grep confirms none exists today (sole definition at eden_help.rs:829), and this is the pin enforcing T-738's banked instruction, so it should scan the crate. (3) eden_help.rs:684-686: a keydown closure that reads NEITHER `ev.key()` NOR `ev.code()`, or whose event parameter is not named `ev`, is silently DROPPED from discovery rather than flagged. Partially mitigated by the declared per-file counts and the empty-bindings check, but 'silently dropped' is the shape the whole census exists to eliminate. (4) eden_dock_left.rs:1527-1537 and :547-550 (T-697): a plain hit that matched on FACTION reports `field` as the entity's first text attribute, so the row title claims `matched name "..."` when the faction is what matched. Cosmetic and never wrong about WHICH entity matched, only about why. Diagnosis: editor_verify/wave119.md NIT-1..4.
tickets.notes: filed by wave-119 adversarial verifier (editor factory)

tickets.title: Paste and place-composition land every slot at z = 0.0 — NEEDS OPERATOR DECISION alongside T-743
tickets.summary: MINOR from the wave-127 focused re-verifier. THIS IS THE ONE WAVE-127 FINDING THAT WAS NOT FIXED, AND IT IS DELIBERATE: it sits on T-743's reserved decision surface. Wave 127 closed a four-instance family where an x/y write with z=None made `update_slot_position` store `pz = 0.0` (store.rs:2779-2783) with nothing re-sampling terrain afterwards — fixed at `attrs_update_position`/`_multi` (F-2), `commit_positions` (F-5, reached by Align/Distribute/place-pattern) and the marquee drag (F-6). The re-verifier then proved that family CLOSED (zero `move_entities` frontend callers; exactly one `move_entities_and_vehicles`; five `update_slot_position` sites, three z-resolved and two rotation-only which cannot trip the mutator's `x.is_some() || y.is_some()` arm). WHAT REMAINS IS A DIFFERENT CLASS — a CREATE path, not a missed caller: `editor_ops.rs:642` (`paste_at_cursor`) pushes `zs.push(0.0)` for every pasted slot and explicitly drops `position.z` from the copied extras, and `place_composition` (store.rs:2394/2409) does the same, symmetric for vehicles. Ctrl+V a rooftop entity and the copy lands on the deck. NO AUTHORED WORK IS DESTROYED — there is no cut, the source is untouched, so this is a wrong-landing-position defect rather than the silent corruption the rest of the wave fixed. WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED AUTONOMOUSLY: the `zs.push(0.0)` carries the in-code rationale 'DEM not ready — byte-parity with the flat-map case', which is the SAME byte-parity-with-the-JS-oracle argument that makes T-743 (`PASTE_NUDGE` = 20 m, store.rs:4998-4999) an operator decision rather than a slice-sized fix. Both are 'where does a pasted entity land', both are pinned to the JS oracle, and changing z unilaterally could pre-empt whichever of T-743's three paths the operator picks. DECIDE THE TWO TOGETHER. The z axis is arguably independent of the x/y nudge — preserving the source z is compatible with all three T-743 paths — but that is the operator's call to make, not the factory's. Diagnosis: editor_verify/wave127.md, focused re-verification section.
tickets.notes: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-08 — same ruling as T-743: the JS byte-parity was a migration safety net, not a contract. A pasted or composed entity must KEEP ITS AUTHORED Z rather than landing at 0.0. Fix editor_ops.rs paste_at_cursor's `zs.push(0.0)` and place_composition (store.rs) to carry the source z, exactly as wave 127 did for the four move/edit paths. Wave 127's rules still bind: fix at the frontend caller where possible, reuse keep_z_rows()/slot_z(), read z off slots_json (exact f64) and NOT the SoA (f32, omits hidden-layer slots per T-665). Sequence with T-743 — they are one behaviour change on two axes and should land together.

tickets.title: Six more register-at-mount thread_local seams have no lifecycle guard — port the wave-129 idiom
tickets.summary: MAJOR, found during wave 129's fix pass and filed rather than fixed because it spans four files outside that wave's owns. THE DEFECT SHAPE, proven twice in wave 129: a `thread_local` seam registered when a component mounts and never unregistered stays callable after the component dies. Backspace hide-chrome unmounts panels (mission_editor.rs, NO modal guard, and dialogs explicitly survive the hide), after which the stale closure REPORTS SUCCESS -- `true`, or a stale value -- while every `set` writes to DISPOSED signals, which reactive_graph 0.2.14 makes a SILENT NO-OP. A click reports success and does nothing: a dead click by lifecycle rather than by routing. TWO FAILURE MODES, and a naive fix closes only the first: (1) no unregister at all, so the stale hook answers forever; (2) an UNCONDITIONAL unregister, so a REMOUNT that installs before the dead component's cleanup runs is clobbered by that cleanup. VERIFIED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR 2026-08-08, `grep -c` per file -- each has register-at-mount seams and ZERO `ptr_eq` and ZERO `on_cleanup`: apps/website/frontend/src/ruler_tool.rs (RULER_CHAIN, 1 seam); apps/website/frontend/src/los_tool.rs (LOS_STATE, LOS_SAMPLER, VIEWSHED_STATE, 3 seams); apps/website/frontend/src/world_assets/mod.rs (register_render_ctx, 1 seam); apps/website/frontend/src/select_tool.rs (register_editor_selection, 1 seam -- this one is DOCUMENTED as deliberately leaking with the engine, so confirm the intent before changing it rather than assuming). THE FIX IS ALREADY WRITTEN AND SHIPPED TWICE -- port it, do not re-invent: `install_seam`/`unregister_seam` plus the `SeamRegistration` trait at apps/website/frontend/src/validation_panel.rs (wave 129, dac84b03) is the generic form covering four seams; eden_dock_right.rs's `install_select_zone` (f6a2b687) is the single-seam form. Register + `on_cleanup` unregister guarded by `Rc::ptr_eq` so only the LOSING registration is cleared. `on_cleanup` is Send + Sync-bound and `Rc<dyn Fn>` is !Send, so park the Rc in a `StoredValue::new_local` and read it back inside the cleanup -- cleanups run BEFORE arena nodes are removed, so the read is valid, and holding the clone keeps the allocation alive. DO NOT compare a bare `usize` address: the old Rc drops on re-register, so a later hook can be allocated at the freed address and a stale cleanup would wrongly clear it (ABA). For a signal-valued seam use the arena key `==` (slotmap versions its keys, so a recycled slot is not mistaken for its predecessor). ACCEPTANCE, three behavioural cases per seam, as wave 129 pinned them: install -> cleanup -> the read reports honest failure AND the stale hook is not called at all; install(A) -> install(B) -> A's cleanup -> B SURVIVES and still answers; never-installed -> honest failure. Perturb both ways: removing the cleanup must redden case 1, and removing the ptr_eq guard must redden case 2 ALONE -- case 2 is the one a naive fix gets wrong. WHY THIS IS URGENT RATHER THAN TIDY: in wave 129 a fix agent ADDED a new instance of this defect (validation_panel.rs `register_route_probe`) while a sibling agent was fixing the identical shape twelve lines away, and then made row clickability depend on it. The pattern is easy to get wrong and there was no shared idiom; now there is one. Audit every seam you touch and every seam you add.
tickets.notes: filed by the orchestrator during wave 129's fix pass; fix idiom already shipped at validation_panel.rs (dac84b03) and eden_dock_right.rs (f6a2b687)

tickets.title: set_loadout discards the acknowledgement T-770 added, so the history tail fires over writes that never happened
tickets.summary: RESIDUE of T-770 (wave 140), verified by the orchestrator 2026-08-08. T-770's whole point was that `commit_writes` counted closure CALLS rather than sink acknowledgements, so its WARNING arm was unreachable. The core half landed: `MissionDocCore::update_slot_loadout` (crates/map-engine-core/src/doc/store.rs:2784) now returns `bool` and returns `false` when the slot id is not in the document. THE FRONTEND HALF DID NOT. `editor_ops::set_loadout` (apps/website/frontend/src/editor_ops.rs:2005) calls `core.update_slot_loadout(id, loadout_json);` and then hardcodes `true` as the value of `did`, discarding the acknowledgement entirely. CONSEQUENCES, both live: (1) `crate::mission_history::after_local_edit()` fires whenever the OPS_CTX and doc merely EXIST, so a set_loadout against a stale or deleted slot id still marks the mission dirty and mints an undo step over a document that did not change; (2) any receipt built on this path still cannot distinguish a real write from a no-op, which is precisely the defect T-770 was filed to close. FIX: return the mutator's bool out of the closure instead of `true`, so `did` means what its name says, and gate `after_local_edit()` on it. Then check the callers — `arsenal.rs:1253` is the live one — and decide whether a refused write should surface to the operator rather than passing silently. ACCEPTANCE: a test that calls set_loadout with an id that is NOT in the document and asserts no history entry is minted and the mission is not dirtied; perturb by restoring the hardcoded `true` and watch it go red. Note arsenal.rs carries source pins naming `pub fn set_loadout` and its tail line (arsenal.rs:6180, :6205, :4897) — update them honestly, do not delete them.
tickets.notes: residue of T-770 (wave 140); core half shipped, frontend half did not

tickets.title: Connections have no line on the map, so CONN-DEL-001 can only be reached from the panel
tickets.summary: DISCLOSED SCOPE GAP carried from T-768 (wave 140) and confirmed still open after the remediation run. T-768 delivered the connect gesture's pointer half once T-723 fixed the armed-pointerup path, so a connection can now be STARTED and FINISHED on the map. What it did not deliver is a rendered LINE: connections draw nothing, so there is no artifact to click, and CONN-DEL-001 (delete a connection) is reachable only from the panel's Delete control. An author who drew a connection on the map has no way to remove it on the map. THIS IS THE SAME SHAPE T-760 AND T-748 ALREADY CLOSED for markers and comments respectively: both needed a render lane in crates/map-engine-render/src/draw_order.rs plus the rebind tail in apps/website/frontend/src/mission_history.rs, and both are now shipped and can be copied rather than re-derived. RECIPE: add the connection lane to draw_order.rs and engine.rs the way the marker lane was added by T-760; feed it from the document, NOT from a slice's own owns — T-069 and T-672 independently established that a lane fed from a slice's own state goes stale after undo/redo/restore, which is why the feed comes first; then wire pick/hit-testing so a line can be selected, and route Delete through the existing path rather than authoring a second one. ACCEPTANCE: draw a connection, undo, redo, restore from IDB, and confirm the line survives each; then select the line on the map and delete it through the same code path the panel's Delete uses.
tickets.notes: scope gap disclosed by T-768 (wave 140); render lane recipe already shipped by T-760 and T-748

tickets.title: Comments still cannot be composed — PLACE-COMMENT-001's last undelivered clause
tickets.summary: RESIDUE of T-748 (wave 141) and, before it, T-651 (wave 114). The spec row PLACE-COMMENT-001 asks for comments that are 'Draggable, copy/paste, layerable, COMPOSABLE' plus a 'Comment icon at position'. T-748 (wave 141) delivered the map glyph, so the icon clause is closed. THE COMPOSABLE CLAUSE IS NOT: compositions capture from the SELECTION, and comments sit in no selection lane, so a comment can never be part of a composition. T-748's own diagnosis called this out — 'composable was a silent drop, which is what the HARD GATE bars' — and it is scope accounting rather than broken code: nothing misbehaves, the feature simply does not exist. THE INTERESTING QUESTION IS WHERE TO PUT COMMENTS. They are deliberately absent from the compiled mission (the same property that keeps them out of the render SoA before T-748 gave them a glyph), so a composition containing a comment must carry it as authoring metadata and must NOT emit it into the compiled output. Check how `place_composition` (crates/map-engine-core/src/doc/store.rs) captures and replays, and whether the comment can ride the same rows without reaching flatten. WATCH THE Z RULE: `place_composition` creates at z = 0.0 (see T-777) and that is on the operator's reserved decision surface with T-743 — do not change paste/composition landing semantics as part of this ticket; carry whatever the operator decides. ACCEPTANCE: select a comment together with entities, make a composition, place it, and confirm the comment comes back at the right offset, survives undo/redo/restore, and does NOT appear in the compiled mission.
tickets.notes: WIDENED 2026-08-08 by the operator's paste ruling. In addition to the composable clause, this ticket now owns the COMPOSITION Z: place_composition hard-codes `position_any(wx, wy, 0.0, rot)` in ALL THREE arms (slot, vehicle, object) in crates/map-engine-core/src/doc/store.rs. T-777 deferred it here explicitly because store.rs was a sibling's file that wave. The operator ruled (T-743/T-777) that the JS byte-parity was a migration safety net, not a contract, and that a pasted entity keeps its authored elevation — the same reasoning applies to a placed composition. Nothing re-samples terrain afterwards (terrainZ died with the React deletion), so a 0.0 written here is final. Wave-127 rules bind: reuse slot_z, read exact f64 rows and NOT the f32 SoA (which omits hidden-layer slots per T-665), and if you build a zs vector prove zs[i] matches ids[i] structurally.

tickets.title: Resolve the player-count question: the editor shows placed slots; the library shows per-side and total
tickets.summary: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-08, closing the T-694 player-cap question that has been open since wave 113. THE RULING: in the EDITOR the figure an author sees is HOW MANY SLOTS ARE PLACED DOWN — the derived count, not an author-typed cap. In the MISSION LIBRARY a mission should show how many slots there are PER SIDE and the TOTAL. CURRENT STATE, verified by the orchestrator: two numbers exist and nothing reconciles them. `max_players` (dto.rs ~:851) is AUTHOR-DECLARED — typed once into the create dialog — and is copied into the compiled mission by `compiled_meta`, so it is not dead. `MissionDocCore::slot_count` is the number of seats the document actually contains. The editor currently shows BOTH side by side and deliberately does not resolve the disagreement; the rationale lives at `eden_settings::PLAYER_COUNT_DISAGREE_NOTE`. This ruling resolves it: slot_count is the truth for the editor's player figure. This is consistent with the operator's wave-113 decision (derived slot count, no min_players). EDITOR HALF (do now): make the derived slot count the figure the author sees, and retire the disagree-note in favour of the decided answer rather than leaving a note explaining an unresolved argument. Do NOT delete `max_players` — it reaches the compiled mission. ONE SUB-QUESTION LEFT FOR THE OPERATOR, do not invent it: should `max_players` remain author-typed at all, or be DERIVED from slot_count so the compiled mission cannot disagree with the document? The ruling settles what is displayed; it does not settle what is compiled. LIBRARY HALF (design deferred by the operator): show slots per side plus the total on the mission library view. The operator explicitly said the exact presentation is to be worked out later — bring a proposal, do not guess at layout. Note the per-side breakdown does not exist as a derived value yet; check whether flatten or the doc can produce it without a new wire field before assuming a schema change.
tickets.notes: closes the T-694 player-cap question; editor half actionable now, library presentation deferred to the operator

tickets.title: The seam lifecycle idiom exists twice — lift install_seam beside the trait it shares
tickets.summary: Loose end disclosed by the T-778 slice (wave 142), filed rather than chased across a file it did not own. Wave 129 built the register-at-mount lifecycle idiom in validation_panel.rs: a `SeamRegistration` identity trait plus `install_seam` / `unregister_seam`, which register a thread_local hook and unregister it at `on_cleanup` behind an `Rc::ptr_eq` guard so only the LOSING registration is cleared. Wave 142 ported it to four more seams in ruler_tool.rs, los_tool.rs and world_assets/mod.rs. THE PROBLEM: `SeamRegistration` is `pub(crate)` and IS shared, but `install_seam` / `unregister_seam` are module-private to validation_panel.rs, so the T-778 slice had to COPY the six-line mechanism into ruler_tool.rs (chosen as host because it is the only one of its files that compiles natively and is visible to the other two). The crate now has ONE identity check and TWO copies of the mechanism that uses it. A duplicated vocabulary is a defect class this repo treats as its own, and this one guards a defect family that has already been found five times in one wave and INTRODUCED once by a fix agent. FIX: lift `install_seam` and `unregister_seam` to `pub(crate)` beside `SeamRegistration` (or into a small module both files can see), repoint validation_panel.rs and ruler_tool.rs at the single definition, and DELETE the copy. Marked in-source as a FOLLOW-UP at ruler_tool.rs. ACCEPTANCE: the crate contains exactly one `fn install_seam` and one `fn unregister_seam` — pin that count, unscoped, over live code — and all existing seam lifecycle tests in both files stay green, including the remount-guard case that must redden ALONE when the ptr_eq guard is removed. NOTE the second loose end from the same slice, NOT in scope here and reported separately: RENDER_CTX (world_assets/mod.rs) has no behavioural test at all because that module is wasm32-only and the crate has no wasm-bindgen-test target; it is covered by a source pin only, which wave 142's verifier showed greens on a decoy identifier.
tickets.notes: loose end disclosed by the T-778 slice (wave 142); the idiom is shipped twice, the fix is a lift and a delete

tickets.title: A comment cannot be selected by clicking it — not on the map, not in the outliner
tickets.summary: OPERATOR-REQUESTED 2026-08-08, off the T-781 slice's own found_not_fixed. T-781 (wave 144) made comments composable and T-748 (wave 141) gave them a map glyph — but NOTHING PUTS A COMMENT ID INTO THE SELECTION BY CLICKING. Verified by the orchestrator on both surfaces: (1) the outliner's comment row is `ROW_STATIC` (apps/website/frontend/src/eden_tree.rs ~:792) — it supports drag-into-folder and dblclick-to-edit, but no click path reaches `ctx.selection`, unlike a slot row which uses the interactive class and calls `editor_ops::select_slot`; (2) the map glyph has NO pick path — a grep for comment hit-testing in mission_editor.rs returns nothing. CONSEQUENCE — CORRECTED BY THE WAVE-144 VERIFIER, WHICH FOUND THE GAP IS TOTAL, NOT PARTIAL: there is currently NO UI lane at all that puts a comment into a selection. This ticket first said the T-697 selection-filter apply was a lane; it is not — its sole caller only NARROWS an existing selection, so it cannot introduce a comment that was never selected. The search router additionally has no comment arm, so comment hits render inert. Capture and place are correct and tested (T-781); they are simply unreachable by a user. The operator asked for this fixed rather than filed. FIX, two halves. OUTLINER: make the comment row selectable the way a slot row is; the affordance and the click must be the SAME decision (wave 129's invariant — a row is clickable IFF clicking it does something). MAP: hit-test the glyph. T-780 (wave 142) is the precedent to copy, not re-derive — it added `pick_connection` (nearest point-to-segment within a tolerance) fed from the SAME function that feeds the render lane, so what is drawn and what a click can find are one set by construction. Do the same for the glyph: one document read feeding both. ⚠️ SELECTION RECONCILE IS THE TRAP HERE, AND IT HAS BITTEN TWICE. Wave 129 found dead clicks from an affordance that did not ask the router; wave 142's F-1 found an edge selection and an entity selection coexisting, so Delete removed the wrong thing. `editor_ops::mirror_selection` is now the ONE writer every entity-selection write funnels through, and it reconciles the map's edge selection. A comment selection must join that reconcile — decide and pin whether a comment selection is exclusive with an entity selection or composes with it, and make it true by CONSTRUCTION rather than by convention. Delete with a comment selected must remove the comment and nothing else. ACCEPTANCE: click a comment in the outliner and on the map — it selects, and it is the thing Delete removes; select a comment together with entities and compose them (the T-781 lane, now reachable without the search filter); the affordance matches the click for every row kind, with a non-vacuity assert that the test saw both selectable and inert rows.
tickets.notes: operator asked for this fixed, not filed; T-780's pick_connection is the map-side precedent, wave 142 F-1 is the reconcile trap
